title: ‘A Knife to the Throat’: Putin’s Logic for Invading Ukraine

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日商业与政策通讯《DealBook》的记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，可以下载

sentences.en: New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的使用权。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: As the world has waited to see whether Russia will or will not invade Ukraine, and with early signs
sentences.zh: 正当世界一直在观望俄罗斯究竟会不会入侵乌克兰，且已有迹象表明

sentences.en: that an invasion may now have begun, much of the uncertainty has hinged on the question of what exactly Vladimir Putin is thinking.
sentences.zh: 入侵可能已经开始之际，许多不确定性都取决于弗拉基米尔·普京究竟在想什么这一问题。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Anton Troianovsky says that the answer may lie in an unusual speech that Putin delivered on Monday night.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事安东·特罗亚诺夫斯基表示，答案可能就藏在普京周一晚间发表的一场不同寻常的演讲中。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, February 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月23日，星期三。

sentences.en: Anton, set the scene for us as this major speech from Vladimir Putin gets underway.
sentences.zh: 安东，请为我们还原弗拉基米尔·普京这场重磅演讲拉开帷幕时的情景。

sentences.en: Well, it's almost 10 p.m.
sentences.zh: 好的，当时快到晚上10点了。

sentences.en: in Moscow on Monday night when state television breaks into regular programming and shows Putin sitting in the Kremlin in a nondescript wood-paneled office,
sentences.zh: 周一晚上的莫斯科，国家电视台插播常规节目，画面显示普京坐在克里姆林宫一间毫不起眼的木镶板办公室里，

sentences.en: Russian flags behind him, a bank of telephones to his left.
sentences.zh: 身后是俄罗斯国旗，左手边是一排电话。

sentences.en: And he starts to deliver a speech that's certainly the most remarkable speech I've seen him give in the time I've been in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他开始发表了一场演讲，这绝对是我在莫斯科期间听过他发表的最引人注目的演讲。

sentences.en: Remarkable why?
sentences.zh: 为什么说引人注目？

sentences.en: You know, it was this emotion, this sense of grievance, even this anger that you could see breaking through again and again as he spoke for almost an hour, and that we haven't seen
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种情绪、那种受委屈的感觉，甚至那种愤怒，在他将近一个小时的讲话中一次又一次地流露出来，而这是我们过去多年来

sentences.en: to this degree in Putin's public appearances over the years.
sentences.zh: 在普京的公开露面中从未见过的。

sentences.en: You would see flashes of it, but to have him speaking to an hour, addressing the nation on national television in prime time, it was really something new, something different.
sentences.zh: 你以前可能会看到一些蛛丝马迹，但让他发表一个小时的讲话，在黄金时段通过国家电视台向全国发表讲话，这真的是一件新事物，有些不一样。

sentences.en: And at a very high level, Anton, what is the goal of this speech?
sentences.zh: 安东，从宏观层面来看，这场演讲的目的是什么？

sentences.en: Well, that's another thing that made this speech so remarkable is that tensions were so incredibly high.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这也是让这场演讲如此引人注目的另一个原因，因为当时局势极其紧张。

sentences.en: You had the sense that after months of buildup, Putin would finally reveal his plans for Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，经过几个月的酝酿，普京终于要公布他对乌克兰的计划了。

sentences.en: Was he going to invade?
sentences.zh: 他会入侵吗？

sentences.en: What goals was he pursuing?
sentences.zh: 他在追求什么目标？

sentences.en: And leading up to this, there was a lot of tension, and the Kremlin had really left this question wide open.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，存在着巨大的紧张局势，克里姆林宫确实将这个问题悬而未决。

sentences.en: What did
sentences.zh: 普京

sentences.en: Putin actually want?
sentences.zh: 究竟想要什么？

sentences.en: And there was a sense, well, maybe we're about to finally find out.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉是，嗯，也许我们终于要找到答案了。

sentences.en: Right, which is why, Anton, we wanted to talk through this speech with you, because it feels like
sentences.zh: 没错，安东，这就是为什么我们想和你一起探讨这场演讲，因为感觉

sentences.en: really it's our best chance of answering the question that pretty much the entire world has right now.
sentences.zh: 这真的是我们回答目前几乎全世界都在关心的问题的最佳机会。

sentences.en: How is Vladimir Putin thinking about Ukraine and about whether to invade it?
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京是如何看待乌克兰以及是否要入侵乌克兰的？

sentences.en: And so we want to have you focus in on a few key passages from this speech as a way of doing that and to
sentences.zh: 因此，我们希望让你重点关注这场演讲中的几个关键段落，以此来做到这一点，并

sentences.en: explain not just what Putin says here, but what he really means, especially given the subtext that is probably lost on non-Russians and on non-Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 解释普京在这里所说的不仅是什么，还有他真正的意思，特别是考虑到非俄罗斯人和非乌克兰人可能无法领会的潜台词。

sentences.en: So with that in mind, where should we start?
sentences.zh: 考虑到这一点，我们应该从哪里开始？

sentences.en: Well, we should start at the beginning, which was this very lengthy, distorted history lesson that
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们应该从头开始，这是一堂非常漫长且被歪曲的历史课，

sentences.en: laid out a historical rationale for, by all appearances, is Putin preparing his nation for potential military action against Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 为普京显然是在为针对乌克兰的潜在军事行动做准备的民族，奠定了历史基础。

sentences.en: He starts in medieval times.
sentences.zh: 他从中世纪讲起。

sentences.en: Since ancient times, people from ancient southwestern Russian lands were calling themselves
sentences.zh: 自古以来，古代俄罗斯西南部土地上的人们就自称为

sentences.en: Russians and Orthodox.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人和东正教徒。

sentences.en: That was happening until 17th century when part of these territories...
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续到17世纪，当时这些领土的一部分……

sentences.en: He talks about this idea that what's present-day Ukraine largely consists of historically Russian lands, that people who lived there centuries ago called themselves Russians.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了这样一种观点，即现今的乌克兰很大程度上由历史上属于俄罗斯的土地组成，几个世纪前生活在那里的人们自称为俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: He then moves on to the early years of the Soviet Union, of the Russian Revolution, and the years after that, when he says
sentences.zh: 然后他谈到了苏联早期、俄国革命以及之后的几年，他说

sentences.en: Lenin and Stalin basically created present-day Ukraine in its present boundaries by granting it all these lands, like Eastern Ukraine, that are really and truly Russian.
sentences.zh: 列宁和斯大林基本上通过将乌克兰东部等所有这些真正属于俄罗斯的土地划给它，在现有的边界内创造了现代乌克兰。

sentences.en: And we have every reason to say now that it's Ukraine created by Vladimir Lenin.
sentences.zh: 我们现在完全有理由说，这是弗拉基米尔·列宁创造的乌克兰。

sentences.en: He is its creator and architect.
sentences.zh: 他是其创造者和总设计师。

sentences.en: And what is he up to here, Putin, with these references?
sentences.zh: 普京引用这些历史意欲何为？

sentences.en: I mean, we've heard a lot of this from him before, but it's really making it clear that
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们以前听他讲过很多次，但这确实表明，

sentences.en: he sees himself in what he's doing now, writing a historical wrong, a historical wrong that goes back essentially more than a century.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己现在的所作所为是在纠正一个历史错误，一个基本上可以追溯到一个多世纪前的历史错误。

sentences.en: And the historical wrong is that actions of Russian Soviet
sentences.zh: 这个历史错误就是俄罗斯苏维埃

sentences.en: Soviet leaders, a century ago, separated the Russian people into what became different countries.
sentences.zh: 苏维埃领导人在一个世纪前的行动，将俄罗斯人民分裂成了后来不同的国家。

sentences.en: He's saying that present-day Ukraine was populated in large part by Russians, by people who considered
sentences.zh: 他说，现代乌克兰很大一部分人口是俄罗斯人，是那些认为自己是

sentences.en: themselves Russians, and that by creating these ethnically defined republics, as the Soviets did
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人的人，并且通过像苏维埃在其早期那样建立这些按种族划分的共和国，

sentences.en: in their early years, that they were thus separating the Russian people, laying a time bomb, as he called it, that then exploded after the Soviet breakup in 1991.
sentences.zh: 他们从而分裂了俄罗斯人民，埋下了一颗定时炸弹（正如他所说），这颗炸弹在1991年苏联解体后爆炸了。

sentences.en: So interestingly, Putin is, in a way, faulting previous Russian leaders for decisions they made that
sentences.zh: 因此有趣的是，普京在某种程度上是在指责前俄罗斯领导人做出的决定，正是这些决定

sentences.en: gave Ukraine a national identity, which clearly Putin thinks was a mistake to have ever done.
sentences.zh: 赋予了乌克兰民族身份，普京显然认为这样做是一个错误。

sentences.en: And he's using this history lesson, accurately or inaccurately, to say that Ukraine and its people really belong to Russia.
sentences.zh: 他借用这段历史（无论准确与否），声称乌克兰及其人民实际上属于俄罗斯。

sentences.en: That's very much the message, yes.
sentences.zh: 这确实是传达的核心信息，是的。

sentences.en: And a bit later in the speech, he brings it up to the present day in this very ominous way by bringing up a process that Ukraine has been going through in recent years called
sentences.zh: 在演讲稍后的部分，他以一种极其不祥的方式将其带入当下，提到了乌克兰近年来经历的一个过程，叫做

sentences.en: decommunization.
sentences.zh: 去共产主义化。

sentences.en: And what does that mean, decommunization?
sentences.zh: 去共产主义化是什么意思？

sentences.en: So decommunization is this process that Ukraine started going through after their pro-Western revolution
sentences.zh: 去共产主义化是乌克兰在2014年亲西方革命后开始经历的一个过程，

sentences.en: in 2014 that involved things like tearing down all the Lenin statues, changing names of cities that were named after Soviet figures.
sentences.zh: 其中包括拆除所有列宁雕像、更改以苏联人物命名的城市名称等事情。

sentences.en: Then Putin brings that up, talks about Ukrainians as ungrateful for knocking down all these Lenin statues.
sentences.zh: 然后普京提到了这一点，指责乌克兰人推倒所有这些列宁雕像的行为忘恩负义。

sentences.en: And then he delivers this line, looking straight at the camera, talking really tough.
sentences.zh: 接着，他直视镜头，用非常严厉的语气说出了这样一番话。

sentences.en: And he says, you want decommunization?
sentences.zh: 他说，你们想要去共产主义化吗？

sentences.en: Well, we are quite happy with that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们对此非常高兴。

sentences.en: But don't stop halfway.
sentences.zh: 但不要半途而废。

sentences.en: You want decommunization?
sentences.zh: 你们想要去共产主义化吗？

sentences.en: Well, this suits us just fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这正合我们心意。

sentences.en: But why stop halfway?
sentences.zh: 但为什么要半途而废呢？

sentences.en: We are ready to show you what would mean actual decommunization for Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我们准备向你们展示对乌克兰来说真正的去共产主义化意味着什么。

sentences.en: We are ready to show you what real decommunization would mean for Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我们准备向你们展示对乌克兰而言真正的去共产主义化意味着什么。

sentences.en: And that was just a clear threat to essentially dismember the country, to say, okay, well,
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个威胁，实质上是要肢解这个国家，意思是，好吧，

sentences.en: then we can take away all the territory that, in Putin's telling, rightfully belongs to Russia and that the communists mistakenly gave to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 那么我们可以拿走所有按照普京的说法本属于俄罗斯、而共产党人错误地赠予乌克兰的领土。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which could mean the whole Black Sea coaSt. It could mean eastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着整个黑海海岸。这可能意味着乌克兰东部。

sentences.en: It could even mean Kiev, which Russians see as the birthplace, essentially, of their civilization.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能意味着基辅，俄罗斯人将基辅视为他们文明的发源地。

sentences.en: So what Putin is saying here, and it's a threat, is if Ukrainians want to rid themselves of their
sentences.zh: 所以普京在这里所说的是一个威胁，如果乌克兰人想要摆脱他们的共产主义历史，

sentences.en: communist history, then they should also rid themselves of the Ukrainian territory that Russia granted them during the communist era.
sentences.zh: 那么他们也应该摆脱俄罗斯在共产主义时期赠予他们的乌克兰领土。

sentences.en: He's offering a rationale for basically invading
sentences.zh: 他正在为基本上入侵

sentences.en: Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰提供理由。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because he's saying, we can do it for you if you don't want to do it yourself.
sentences.zh: 因为他在说，如果你们自己不想做，我们可以代劳。

sentences.en: We can take away the land for you.
sentences.zh: 我们可以为你们收回这片土地。

sentences.en: So ultimately, this is as much an emotional argument as it is a historical one for why
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这是一个情感论点，也是一个历史论点，用来解释为什么

sentences.en: Putin, in his mind, should be able to send troops into Ukraine, which is that Ukraine isn't real.
sentences.zh: 在普京看来，他有理由向乌克兰派兵，因为乌克兰不是真的。

sentences.en: It's not a legitimate nation.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个合法的国家。

sentences.en: It's just a historical part of Russia.
sentences.zh: 它只是俄罗斯的一个历史组成部分。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And Putin takes that argument a step further.
sentences.zh: 普京将这一论点进一步推演。

sentences.en: And calls Ukraine basically a colony of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 基本上把乌克兰称作西方的殖民地。

sentences.en: You know, Putin says he doesn't want to literally rebuild the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 你知道，普京说他并非字面意义上想要重建苏联。

sentences.en: Putin says he doesn't want to reattach all the 14 former Soviet republics that aren't Russia back to Russia.
sentences.zh: 普京说他并不想把除俄罗斯之外的所有14个前苏联加盟共和国重新并入俄罗斯。

sentences.en: But he says
sentences.zh: 但他说

sentences.en: Ukraine is different.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰情况不同。

sentences.en: Ukraine is particularly illegitimate because of the pro-Western revolution that happened there in 2014.
sentences.zh: 由于2014年那里发生了亲西方革命，乌克兰尤其缺乏合法性。

sentences.en: To most of the world, you know, it was a genuine uprising against a
sentences.zh: 对世界上大多数人来说，你知道，这是一场针对

sentences.en: Russia-friendly leader who went back on plans to get closer to the European Union.
sentences.zh: 亲俄领导人的真正起义，该领导人背叛了与欧盟走得更近的计划。

sentences.en: But to Putin, that was an armed coup in 2014 into coup d'etat.
sentences.zh: 但在普京看来，那是2014年的一场武装政变和一次政变。

sentences.en: And a front, essentially, for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 本质上是美国

sentences.en: and American efforts to undermine Russia.
sentences.zh: 以及美国破坏俄罗斯努力的幌子。

sentences.en: So first, he's arguing it's illegitimate because, historically speaking, it's part of Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，他争辩说它不合法，因为从历史的角度来看它是俄罗斯的一部分。

sentences.en: Now he's manufacturing this case that it's illegitimate because it's secretly being run by the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 现在他又捏造了这样一种情况，即它不合法，因为它是由西方在暗中操纵的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it also dovetails with that paranoia that you see in Putin and the security establishment around him, this idea that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的，这也与普京及其周围安全建制派中存在的这种偏执狂相吻合，这种观点认为美国

sentences.en: is always out to get us.
sentences.zh: 总是想方设法对付我们。

sentences.en: Anytime we see the U.S.
sentences.zh: 每当我们看到美国

sentences.en: supporting pro-democracy movements in the former Soviet regions, that that is necessarily an attempt to essentially undermine Russia.
sentences.zh: 支持前苏联地区的亲民主运动时，那必然是企图从根本上破坏俄罗斯的稳定。

sentences.en: And so then Putin goes from that to this even more inflammatory claim.
sentences.zh: 于是普京从这一点出发，提出了一个更具煽动性的主张。

sentences.en: The idea that Ukraine is carrying out a genocide against Russian speakers in eastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰正在对乌克兰东部的俄语人口实施种族灭绝的观点。

sentences.en: And our Western colleagues proclaim themselves as the only representatives of this free world.
sentences.zh: 我们的西方同事自诩为这个自由世界的唯一代表。

sentences.en: They prefer not to notice this, as if there is nothing like this happening.
sentences.zh: 他们选择对此视而不见，就好像根本没有发生过这种事一样。

sentences.en: There is no genocide perpetuated against almost 14 million people.
sentences.zh: 没有对近1400万人实施种族灭绝。

sentences.en: Ukraine has passed laws promoting the Ukrainian language, something that has infuriated some people
sentences.zh: 乌克兰通过了推广乌克兰语的法律，这激怒了俄罗斯的一些人，

sentences.en: in Russia who say that the Russian language should be equally promoted in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他们认为俄语也应该在乌克兰得到同等的推广。

sentences.en: But of course, the idea of a genocide, the idea of any kind of mass killing going on in Ukraine is completely false.
sentences.zh: 但当然，种族灭绝的说法，乌克兰发生任何形式的大规模屠杀的说法都是完全错误的。

sentences.en: But it is something that helps Putin even further build the case here in Russia of the Ukrainian government being illegitimate, being a danger to Russians all over the world.
sentences.zh: 但这确实有助于普京在俄罗斯进一步渲染乌克兰政府不合法、是全世界俄罗斯人威胁的论调。

sentences.en: So we're seeing a kind of kitchen sink approach where elements of history that are true are being
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到了一种“厨房水槽式”（无所不包）的方法，即真实的歷史元素

sentences.en: mingled with hyperbolic and in some cases completely false arguments about why Ukraine is not legitimate and why he thinks he should be able to roll in with troops and tanks.
sentences.zh: 与夸大其词、甚至在某些情况下完全错误的论点交织在一起，以此来解释为什么乌克兰不合法，以及为什么他认为自己可以派军队和坦克长驱直入。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, the troops and tanks part is left unsaid in this speech.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这场演讲中没有明说派军队和坦克的事。

sentences.en: But in this context that we're in right now of fearing a Russian invasion, that is very much the message here.
sentences.zh: 但在我们目前担心俄罗斯入侵的背景下，这正是这里传达的核心信息。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Anton, what's the next section of Putin's speech that stands out to you and that we should focus on?
sentences.zh: 安东，普京演讲的下一部分有哪些让你印象深刻、我们应该重点关注的内容？

sentences.en: So he pivots from making this historical and ethnic case against Ukrainian independence to one centered on Russian security, something that he is obviously deeply passionate about.
sentences.zh: 因此，他将话题从针对乌克兰独立的民族和历史论据，转向了以俄罗斯安全为中心的论据，这是他显然极为热衷的一个问题。

sentences.en: And if Ukraine was to join NATO, would serve as a direct threat to the security of Russia.
sentences.zh: 如果乌克兰加入北约，将对俄罗斯的安全构成直接威胁。

sentences.en: He centers on the fact that Ukraine has pursued membership in NATO, the Western alliance that's led by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他把重点放在乌克兰一直在寻求加入北约上，北约是由美国主导的西方同盟。

sentences.en: And NATO has said that Ukraine will become a NATO member, but it's clear also that that's not going to happen anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 北约曾表示乌克兰将成为北约成员国，但显而易见的是，这不会在短期内发生。

sentences.en: But to Putin...
sentences.zh: 但对普京而言……

sentences.en: We say, OK, it is not going to happen tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们说，好吧，它明天不会发生。

sentences.en: But the day after tomorrow, then, what will it change?
sentences.zh: 但如果是后天呢，那又会改变什么？

sentences.en: In historical context, nothing.
sentences.zh: 在历史背景下，什么也不会改变。

sentences.en: The fact that it's not going to happen anytime soon is not that important.
sentences.zh: 它不会在短期内发生这一事实并不那么重要。

sentences.en: He sees just the very possibility of Ukraine's NATO membership in his telling as a fundamental threat to Russian security.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，乌克兰加入北约的这种可能性本身就是对俄罗斯安全的根本威胁。

sentences.en: You know, he sees it as kind of the apotheosis, the worst part of the waves of eastward expansion of NATO that we've seen over the last couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他认为这是过去几十年来我们所看到的北约一再向东扩张的最高峰、最糟糕的部分。

sentences.en: At one point in the speech, he actually addresses the U.S.
sentences.zh: 演讲中的某一点，他实际上直接向美国喊话。

sentences.en: OK, you don't want to see a friend in us, an ally in us.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你们不想把我们当成朋友，把我们当成盟友。

sentences.en: But why do you want to make an enemy out of us?
sentences.zh: 但你们为什么要树敌于我们？

sentences.en: He says, why was it necessary to make an enemy out of us?
sentences.zh: 他说，为什么非要把我们变成敌人？

sentences.en: Sort of saying, why did you have to expand so much in our direction?
sentences.zh: 有点像在说，你们为什么非要朝我们的方向扩张得这么厉害？

sentences.en: And then he goes on to answer that himself.
sentences.zh: 接着他自己回答了这个问题。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: they don't need such a big and independent country as Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要像俄罗斯这么大、这么独立的国家。

sentences.en: Well, it's because the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是因为美国

sentences.en: didn't want such a large independent country as Russia, underscoring his point that a central pillar of American policy is allegedly weakening Russia.
sentences.zh: 不希望俄罗斯这样一个庞大的独立国家存在，他以此强调美国政策的核心支柱之一据称是削弱俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Antonis, is he right to argue that?
sentences.zh: 安东尼斯，他这样辩称对吗？

sentences.en: I mean, when you think about
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你想到

sentences.en: NATO's expansion over the past few decades, it has moved east and taken in countries that are closer and closer to Russia.
sentences.zh: 过去几十年北约的扩张，它一直在向东推进，吸纳了越来越靠近俄罗斯的国家。

sentences.en: And knowing that the history of NATO is that it comes into existence to keep
sentences.zh: 并且知道北约存在的历史就是为了

sentences.en: Russia in Czech.
sentences.zh: 遏制俄罗斯。

sentences.en: That's just the history of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的历史。

sentences.en: Is Putin right to see the eastward expansion of NATO as a kind of provocation and a threat?
sentences.zh: 普京将北约东扩视为一种挑衅和威胁，他这样做对吗？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, those countries that joined NATO, like Poland, like the Baltic states,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，那些加入北约的国家，比如波兰、波罗的海国家，

sentences.en: saw Russia as a threat and saw NATO membership as sort of key to their sovereignty and independence.
sentences.zh: 将俄罗斯视为威胁，并将北约成员身份视为其主权和独立的某种关键。

sentences.en: And of course, the NATO alliance describes itself as a defensive alliance that does not threaten Russia.
sentences.zh: 当然，北约联盟将自己描述为一个不威胁俄罗斯的防御性联盟。

sentences.en: But yes, of course, it's not just Putin here in Moscow that sees NATO as a threat.
sentences.zh: 但没错，当然，在莫斯科这里，不仅仅是普京将北约视为威胁。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: World War II was ended only 77 years ago.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战结束仅仅77年前。

sentences.en: And that was obviously an invasion from the West by Nazi Germany that caused monumental, incredible harm.
sentences.zh: 那显然是纳粹德国从西方发动的入侵，造成了巨大的、难以置信的伤害。

sentences.en: So yes, NATO expansion is in fact a touchy subject here.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，北约扩张在这里其实是一个敏感的话题。

sentences.en: It's something that annoyed a lot of people in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 这让莫斯科的许多人感到恼火。

sentences.en: But the way that Putin has made fighting NATO expansion so central to his entire foreign policy is really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 但普京将反对北约扩张作为其整个外交政策的核心，这种方式确实引人注目。

sentences.en: And he's punctuating it in this speech by asking the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他在这次演讲中通过向美国发问来强调这一点

sentences.en: why it had to be this way.
sentences.zh: 为什么事情非得是这样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's asking why it had to be this way.
sentences.zh: 他在质问为什么事情非得是这样。

sentences.en: And then, you know, he goes on to talk specifically about what would happen if various missiles were based in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，他接着具体谈到了如果各种导弹部署在乌克兰会发生什么。

sentences.en: You know, you can tell he's spent an enormous time thinking about this and studying this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，看得出来他花了很多时间思考和研究这个问题。

sentences.en: He says, well, if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，如果美国

sentences.en: were to base a Tomahawk cruise missile in Ukraine, it could hit Moscow within 35 minutes.
sentences.zh: 在乌克兰部署战斧巡航导弹，它可能在35分钟内击中莫斯科。

sentences.en: If it was a ballistic missile, it could hit Moscow within seven minutes.
sentences.zh: 如果是弹道导弹，它可能在七分钟内击中莫斯科。

sentences.en: If it was a hypersonic missile, it could be four minutes or five minutes.
sentences.zh: 如果是高超音速导弹，可能只要四分钟或五分钟。

sentences.en: So obviously, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，美国

sentences.en: says it has no plans to put such weapons in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 表示没有计划在乌克兰部署此类武器。

sentences.en: But again, you see how central this perceived threat is to Putin.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，你可以看到这种感受到的威胁对普京而言是多么核心。

sentences.en: So just to be clear, Putin is saying if Ukraine were to someday join NATO and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以为了说清楚，普京是在说，如果乌克兰有朝一日加入北约，而美国

sentences.en: were to put weapon systems in Ukraine, he's calculating in his head the risks that that would present to his government in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 在乌克兰部署武器系统，他正在心里计算这会给他在莫斯科的政府带来的风险。

sentences.en: And it sounds like he's literally counting the minutes that it would take for a missile in Ukraine to reach him.
sentences.zh: 听起来他简直是在计算乌克兰的导弹飞到他这里所需要的分钟数。

sentences.en: The direct quote, what Putin said there was,
sentences.zh: 直接引语，普京当时说的是，

sentences.en: it is like a knife to the throat.
sentences.zh: 这就好比一把尖刀架在喉咙上。

sentences.en: That's how he sees it.
sentences.zh: 他是这么看的。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of language he uses on this issue.
sentences.zh: 这也是他在这个问题上使用的语言。

sentences.en: And so this becomes yet another justification for taking military action against Ukraine to keep it
sentences.zh: 因此，这成了对乌克兰采取军事行动的又一个借口，旨在将其

sentences.en: out of NATO and therefore prevent weapons that could reach him in 35 or 15 minutes from ever getting put by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 排除在北约之外，从而防止美国将能够在35分钟或15分钟内击中他的武器

sentences.en: in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 部署在乌克兰。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, there was another moment in the speech where I really heard him pointing at the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，演讲中还有另一个时刻，我真的听到他把矛头指向美国

sentences.en: as a way of justifying a potential invasion.
sentences.zh: 以此来为潜在的入侵辩护。

sentences.en: And that was a moment where he brought up this really far-fetched idea.
sentences.zh: 那是他提出一个非常荒诞的想法的时刻。

sentences.en: We also heard statements about Ukraine wanting to create their own nuclear weapon.
sentences.zh: 我们还听到关于乌克兰想要制造自己的核武器的声明。

sentences.en: That Ukraine could develop nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 即乌克兰可能会发展核武器。

sentences.en: And he says, if Ukraine has a weapon of mass destruction, the situation in the world, in Europe, especially for us, for Russia, will change drastically.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果乌克兰拥有大规模杀伤性武器，世界局势、欧洲局势，尤其是对我们、对俄罗斯来说，将发生剧烈变化。

sentences.en: If Ukraine acquires weapons of mass destruction, the situation in the world and in Europe will drastically change, especially for us, for Russia.
sentences.zh: 如果乌克兰获得大规模杀伤性武器，世界和欧洲的局势将发生翻天覆地的变化，特别是对我们俄罗斯而言。

sentences.en: We cannot help but react to this real threat.
sentences.zh: 我们不能不对这一现实威胁作出反应。

sentences.en: And I can't imagine that he didn't deliver that line, not thinking about 2003, about Colin Powell and his famous U.N.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象他在发表这段台词时，没有想到2003年，没有想到科林·鲍威尔和他著名的联合国

sentences.en: address.
sentences.zh: 演讲。

sentences.en: That invasion of Iraq by the United States that Russia obviously opposed is something you hear
sentences.zh: 美国对伊拉克的入侵是俄罗斯显然反对的，这是你听到

sentences.en: Putin talking about time and time again.
sentences.zh: 普京一次又一次谈论的事情。

sentences.en: And I think right now what you're seeing is Putin looking back at military action that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为你现在看到的是普京在回顾美国

sentences.en: undertook.
sentences.zh: 采取的军事行动。

sentences.en: You know, the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia in 1999, the invasion of Iraq in 2003.
sentences.zh: 你知道，1999年北约轰炸南斯拉夫，2003年入侵伊拉克。

sentences.en: And he's really saying, you know, he's never said it outright, but that's really what you hear when you read between the lines.
sentences.zh: 他其实是在说，你知道，他从来没有明说，但当你字斟句酌时，听到的确实就是这个意思。

sentences.en: It's if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果美国

sentences.en: did this for what it claimed were its important national security interests or humanitarian reasons, then we should be able to do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 为了其声称的重要国家安全利益或人道主义原因而这么做，那么我们也应该能够做同样的事情。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So when Putin raises the possibility of weapons of mass destruction in Ukraine, which you just
sentences.zh: 所以当普京提出乌克兰存在大规模杀伤性武器的可能性时，也就是你刚刚

sentences.en: called far-fetched, what you're really hearing is Putin saying something else entirely, which is that if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 称为荒诞的事，你真正听到的其实是普京在表达完全不同的另一层意思，那就是如果美国

sentences.en: and its allies can invade a country like Iraq on what turn out to be very shaky grounds, then he should be able to invade a country like Ukraine on whatever grounds he
sentences.zh: 及其盟友可以凭借最终证明是非常站不住脚的理由入侵像伊拉克这样的国家，那么他也可以凭借自己想出的任何理由

sentences.en: comes up with.
sentences.zh: 入侵像乌克兰这样的国家。

sentences.en: Well, he would also say that, you know, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他还会说，你知道，美国

sentences.en: invaded Iraq, a country on the other side of the world, whereas here Putin is talking about a country that is Russia's neighbor.
sentences.zh: 入侵了伊拉克这样一个远在世界另一端的国家，而在这里，普京谈论的是一个作为俄罗斯邻国的国家。

sentences.en: And he's saying, you know, if that country becomes a threat to us, it really is an existential issue.
sentences.zh: 他在说，你知道，如果那个国家对我们构成威胁，这确实是一个生死攸关的问题。

sentences.en: Another thing Putin brings up all the time is the idea of double standards.
sentences.zh: 普京经常提出的另一件事是双重标准的概念。

sentences.en: And so he's saying, well, if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以他在说，好吧，如果美国

sentences.en: can get away with it, then we should be able to do this too.
sentences.zh: 能逃脱惩罚，那我们也能这么做。

sentences.en: So, Anton, how does this speech ultimately end?
sentences.zh: 那么，安东，这场演讲最后是怎么结束的？

sentences.en: Well, this whole nearly hour-long speech has been about historical grievances, ethnic wrongs, issues of Russian security.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这整个将近一小时的演讲都在讲述历史恩怨、民族委屈、俄罗斯的安全问题。

sentences.en: And then at the end, he finally gets to talking about what might come next.
sentences.zh: 然后到了最后，他终于开始谈论接下来可能会发生什么。

sentences.en: Now, almost every day, we are shelling settlements in Donbass.
sentences.zh: 现在，几乎每天，我们都在炮击顿巴斯的定居点。

sentences.en: And he brings up those separatist territories in eastern Ukraine, you know, the ones kind
sentences.zh: 他提到了乌克兰东部的那些分裂主义领土，你知道，那些可以说是

sentences.en: of in the heart of what Putin sees as a rightfully Russian region, one where Russia has backed this separatist movement since 2014.
sentences.zh: 位于普京视为理应属于俄罗斯的地区核心地带的领土，自2014年以来俄罗斯一直在那里支持这个分裂主义运动。

sentences.en: He's been claiming that Ukraine plans an offensive against these separatist territories, that it plans
sentences.zh: 他一直声称乌克兰计划对这些分裂领土发动进攻，计划

sentences.en: to retake them by force, which, by the way, Kyiv is denying having any plans to retake the territories.
sentences.zh: 通过武力重新夺回它们，顺便说一句，基辅方面否认有任何重新夺回这些领土的计划。

sentences.en: And in this very end of the speech, he says a very worrying line.
sentences.zh: 而在演讲的最后，他说了一句非常令人担忧的话。

sentences.en: Kyiv must immediately stop hostilities.
sentences.zh: 基辅必须立即停止敌对行动。

sentences.en: Otherwise, the responsibility for the possible continuation of the bloodshed will lie entirely on the conscience of Ukraine's ruling regime.
sentences.zh: 否则，可能延续流血事件的责任将完全由乌克兰的执政政权承担。

sentences.en: I'm confident that I will have support of the people of Russia, all the patriotic forces of Russia.
sentences.zh: 我相信我会得到俄罗斯人民、俄罗斯所有爱国力量的支持。

sentences.en: Thank you for your attention.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的关注。

sentences.en: So, number one, he's calling it a ruling regime.
sentences.zh: 所以，第一，他称其为一个执政政权。

sentences.en: He's, again, not even recognizing the legitimacy of the government.
sentences.zh: 他再次甚至不承认该政府的合法性。

sentences.en: And number two, of course, he's giving us a preview of the fact that the bloodshed here could continue.
sentences.zh: 第二，当然，他在向我们预告这里的流血事件可能会继续。

sentences.en: And that was classic Putin not telling us what's coming, leaving us guessing, but giving us the sense that what comes next could be really bad.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合普京的风格：不告诉我们接下来会发生什么，让我们去猜，但传达出的感觉是，接下来的事情可能会非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: An image of a very bloody war.
sentences.zh: 一幅充满血腥战争的画面。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So, Anton, what were you thinking when this speech ended and you no doubt sat down and tried to make sense of it?
sentences.zh: 那么，安东，当这场演讲结束，你毫无疑问坐下来试图理解它时，你在想什么？

sentences.en: Well, I have to say it gave me goosebumps.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我必须说这让我起了一身鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: It was this feeling that we had just heard nearly an hour of this, obviously flawed, but very comprehensive argument from multiple directions about why Ukraine right now is a
sentences.zh: 这种感觉就像是我们刚刚听了将近一个小时的这种显然有瑕疵、但从多个角度来看却非常全面的论点，讲述为什么乌克兰现在是

sentences.en: fundamental threat to Russia.
sentences.zh: 对俄罗斯的根本威胁。

sentences.en: Why the situation is something that needs to be addressed with the utmost urgency.
sentences.zh: 为什么局势是一个需要以极其紧迫的态度去处理的问题。

sentences.en: It didn't really leave much room for diplomacy or negotiation or space for concessions for
sentences.zh: 它其实没有给外交或谈判留下太多空间，也没有为普京

sentences.en: Putin to make here.
sentences.zh: 在这里做出让步留下余地。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is not a speech that argues for de-escalation and perhaps Putin is posturing, but it very much
sentences.zh: 这不是一场主张局势降级的演讲，也许普京是在摆姿态，但人们强烈地感到，

sentences.en: feels that what this speech ultimately accomplishes is that it lays the groundwork for major military action in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这场演讲最终实现的效果是，它为在乌克兰采取重大军事行动奠定了基础。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And immediately after that speech, state television cuts to Putin signing a decree that, among other
sentences.zh: 就在那场演讲之后，国家电视台切到了普京签署一项法令的画面，该法令

sentences.en: things, orders the Russian army to carry out, quote unquote, peacekeeping functions in these separatist territories in eastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 除其他事项外，下令俄军在乌克兰东部的这些分裂领土上执行所谓的维和职能。

sentences.en: Then the next day, Putin gets the Russian parliament to authorize the use of military force in Ukraine
sentences.zh: 然后在第二天，普京让俄罗斯议会授权在乌克兰使用军事力量，

sentences.en: and delivers a news conference where he even more directly threatens the possibility of war.
sentences.zh: 并举行了一场新闻发布会，在会上他更加直接地威胁了发生战争的可能性。

sentences.en: So at this point, it's 1 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以此时，是莫斯科时间周三凌晨1点。

sentences.en: Moscow time, Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 周三早晨。

sentences.en: All those forces arrayed around Ukraine have not, as far as we know, crossed into Ukrainian held territory yet.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，部署在乌克兰周边的所有部队尚未越境进入乌克兰控制的领土。

sentences.en: But President Putin has now laid out an extremely comprehensive case for why, in his view, using military force would be justified.
sentences.zh: 但普京总统现在已经提出了一个极其全面的论据，说明在他看来，使用武力将是正当的。

sentences.en: Well, Anton, it is very late there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，安东，那里已经很晚了。

sentences.en: Thank you very much and get some reSt.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，好好休息一下。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: By Tuesday evening, in response to Russia's actions, the United States, the United Nations, and leaders across Europe condemned the government of Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 到周二晚上，为回应俄罗斯的行动，美国、联合国以及欧洲各国的领导人都谴责了弗拉基米尔·普京的政府。

sentences.en: And several of them announced plans to punish it.
sentences.zh: 其中几人宣布了惩罚它的计划。

sentences.en: Germany said it would halt the authorization of a major gas pipeline from Russia called Nord Stream 2.
sentences.zh: 德国表示将暂停批准一条名为“北溪-2”的俄罗斯大型天然气管道。

sentences.en: Canada said it would ban its citizens from engaging in financial transactions with the two Ukrainian regions where Putin has authorized troops.
sentences.zh: 加拿大表示将禁止其公民与普京授权派兵的两个乌克兰地区进行金融交易。

sentences.en: And the Biden administration announced a set of economic sanctions against Russian financial institutions and Russian elites.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府则宣布对俄罗斯金融机构和俄罗斯精英实施一系列经济制裁。

sentences.en: He directly attacked Ukraine's right to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 他直接攻击了乌克兰生存的权利。

sentences.en: In remarks from the White House, Biden specifically cited Putin's Monday night speech, saying it
sentences.zh: 在白宫发表的讲话中，拜登专门引用了普京周一晚上的演讲，称其

sentences.en: made clear that he was uninterested in diplomacy and was bent on aggression toward Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 表明他对外交毫无兴趣，执意对乌克兰进行侵略。

sentences.en: He's setting up a rationale to take more territory by force, in my view.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他正在为通过武力夺取更多领土制造借口。

sentences.en: And if we listened to his speech last night, and many of you did, I know, he's setting up a rationale to go much further.
sentences.zh: 如果我们听了他昨晚的演讲——我知道你们很多人都听了——他正在为走得更远制造借口。

sentences.en: This is the beginning of a Russian invasion of Ukraine, as he indicated and asked permission to be.
sentences.zh: 正如他所暗示并寻求允许的那样，这是俄罗斯入侵乌克兰的开始。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, a jury found the three white men who had already been found guilty of murdering
sentences.zh: 周二，陪审团裁定三名已被判定谋杀

sentences.en: Ahmaud Arbery, guilty of a federal hate crime.
sentences.zh: 艾马德·阿贝里的白人男子犯下联邦仇恨罪。

sentences.en: In doing so, the jury found that the men were motivated by racism.
sentences.zh: 通过这一裁决，陪审团认定这些男子是出于种族主义动机。

sentences.en: When they chased the 25-year-old black man through their neighborhood and shot him to death.
sentences.zh: 当时他们在社区里追逐这名25岁的黑人男子并将其枪杀。

sentences.en: Prosecutors at the Department of Justice had initially resisted holding a hate crimes trial, instead accepting a plea deal from the three men.
sentences.zh: 司法部的检察官最初曾抵制进行仇恨罪审判，而是接受了这三名男子的认罪协议。

sentences.en: But Arbery's family persuaded a federal judge to reject that deal and pursue a trial.
sentences.zh: 但阿贝里的家人说服了一名联邦法官拒绝该协议并进行审判。

sentences.en: I now want to address the members of the DOJ.
sentences.zh: 我现在要向司法部的成员们喊话。

sentences.en: You guys accepted a plea deal with these three murderers who took my son's life.
sentences.zh: 你们竟然接受了与这三名夺走我儿子生命的凶手的认罪协议。

sentences.en: After the guilty verdict, Arbery's mother criticized the federal prosecutors.
sentences.zh: 在有罪判决作出后，阿贝里的母亲批评了联邦检察官。

sentences.en: On what the DOJ did today, they was made to do today.
sentences.zh: 关于司法部今天所做的事，那是逼不得已才做的。

sentences.en: It wasn't because of what they wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 并非出于他们自己的意愿。

sentences.en: They were made to do their job today.
sentences.zh: 他们今天是逼不得已才履行职责的。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Austin Mitchell, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Muj Zadie.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由奥斯汀·米歇尔、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和穆杰·扎迪制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Patricia Willens.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩和帕特里夏·威伦斯剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marion Lozano and Aliciaba Etoop.
sentences.zh: 包含马里恩·洛扎诺和阿利西亚巴·埃图普的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: Of Wunderland.
sentences.zh: 来自沃德兰乐队。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《今日秀》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《割草机秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让您的客人在家中感到宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要完全黑暗才能入睡吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到不省人事才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这非常讲究。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏史或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》App或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听The Wirecutter Show。
